A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, title, and core experiments. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original expert annotations, statistical analyses, LLM close-reading evaluations, and analyses of expert and crowd preferences.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional model comparisons and an empirical random baseline.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Table 4 replace the generation-source random intercept in the creativity regression with fixed categorical source effects. This changes the statistical model, while the annotation framework and core LLM judging procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use the New Yorker fiction study, OLMo-generated passages, GPT-5/Claude-4.1 follow-up, Style Mimic, and LMArena preferences. V2 explicitly aggregates main-study and frontier-study annotations into its 8,618 total; this does not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5 and Figure 4 add Claude-4.5, Gemini-3-Pro, finetuned Gemini-2.5-Pro, and an empirical random baseline to the close-reading comparisons. This substantially expands the comparison set, particularly by introducing a measured chance reference.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 reports removing two passages found in pretraining data and 37 expressions with unstable perplexity estimates. Reported analysis samples change, including 15,982 to 15,725 observations in Table 4. The basic annotation design, 60/40 finetuning split, and 90% expression-matching threshold remain.

E4.justification: The qualitative failure cases are revised: Figure 1 replaces the high-Creativity-Index illustration with two annotated cases distinguishing contextual inappropriateness from nonsensicality, and Table 1 replaces one low-novelty creative example. The crowd-preference and Creativity Index analyses already existed in v1's appendices.

E5.justification: Section 4 adds denominators and Wilson 95% confidence intervals for the headline proportions. Table 2 newly specifies Dunnett adjustment for multiple comparisons. The existing F1 confidence-interval method is retained, with no reported increase in repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: V1's claim that 91% of highly novel expressions were not creative to any annotator becomes a distinction between 91% at annotation level and 79% of unique expressions. Figure 4 adds comparator results, including random F1 scores of 9.6 and 2.3. Regression results also change: GPT-5/human odds ratio becomes 0.511 rather than 0.445, and Table 9's reward coefficient changes from 0.12 with an interval crossing zero to 0.28 with a positive interval. These are revised analyses, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The revised Section 3 equation removes the normally distributed generation-source random effect and introduces fixed source coefficients, changing a formal modeling assumption. The creativity definition and Appendix A.1 sampling mathematics remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the LLM identification claim from creative expressions to expressions perceived as novel, matching the actual task. It also foregrounds the advantage over Creativity Index already discussed in v1 Appendix E. The central claims about novelty's insufficiency and LLM pragmaticality remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains the choice of fiction, clarifies that deliberate pragmatic violations such as surreal writing can be acceptable, and qualifies perfect F1 as requiring agreement with every subjective annotator judgment. It also removes v1's suggestion that failure to recognize non-pragmatic expressions explains their generation.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents quintile-based selection of the existing frontier-study passages, identifies excluded passage IDs and unstable perplexity estimates, and supplies fuller preference-regression specifications in Tables 13–15. Existing prompts, hardware, finetuning settings, and the promised dataset/model release remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Chiang et al., Dunnett, and Kaufman et al. (2008, 2009), and removes the 1966 Levenshtein citation while retaining the cited similarity implementation. The related-work positioning and central distinction from n-gram creativity metrics remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 consistently distinguishes perceived novelty, revises introductory and task explanations, and copyedits the prose. Former Appendices D and E are incorporated into Section 5, and appendix subsections are reorganized, while the overall seven-section narrative remains.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced, Figure 4 expands substantially, and v1 Figure 7 is redrawn and moved into the main text as Figure 5. V2 also adds Tables 13–15, expands regression tables with R-squared rows, and revises plot axes, captions, and figure placement. These materially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 replaces the unsupported random-precision comparison with measured F1 baselines, distinguishes annotation-level from unique-expression percentages, adds uncertainty estimates, and documents data cleaning and fuller regression fits. These improve calibration and transparency. The benefit is tempered by reporting inconsistencies, including 241 creative highlights in Section 2 versus 274 in the conclusion, and the joint-model confidence interval in Table 15 conflicting with the text's p = 0.010.
